query: Prior calculations on concentrated alloys examined variations in atomic mass and force constants, temperature-dependent lattice heat transport, or DFT-derived elastic properties coupled to analytical conductivity estimates; some estimates require a Debye temperature. The cited simulations generally represented perfect, defect-free bulk crystals. Experiments below 200 K indicate that lattice and electronic contributions in HfNbTaTiZr can be comparable, while measurements from 300 to 1200 K on a specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen report total conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m). Available analytical approaches do not capture all relevant atomic-scale complexity in refractory high-entropy alloys, and separate transport studies do not establish a predictive solution for this alloy. Given these constraints, what testable hypothesis could an unspecified new predictive approach make for HfNbTaTiZr without conflating lattice and electronic heat transport? Explain why it should outperform earlier approaches, quantify the expected improvement, define its temperature and sample applicability limits, identify supporting observations from the cited work, and specify decisive comparisons with low- and high-temperature measurements that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A new predictive approach that decouples lattice and electronic contributions—by combining finite‐temperature ab initio calculations (including anharmonic and force constant variations) with Bayesian optimization to refine element‐specific parameters—will predict the lattice thermal conductivity of defect‐free HfNbTaTiZr with at least a 20% reduction in error relative to existing analytical models that conflate both transport mechanisms.
generation.material_initial_state: Defect‐free, homogeneous HfNbTaTiZr alloy (e.g., produced via high‐purity arc melting with minimal contamination and dendritic microstructure), with well‐characterized composition.
generation.intervention: Application of an integrated predictive framework using advanced DFT-based finite temperature methods and Bayesian multi-objective optimization to separately model lattice vibrations (phonon contribution) and electron scattering.
generation.conditions: Measurements conducted at low temperatures (below 200 K) on oxygen‐free or minimally contaminated samples to isolate lattice transport, and additional controlled experiments at high temperatures (300–1200 K) on samples with controlled oxygen content (e.g., 1 wt.% oxygen) for comparison.
generation.structural_mediator: Atomic-scale variations in force constants and anharmonic effects that separately modulate lattice vibrations independent of the electron transport channels.
generation.mechanism: By explicitly calculating temperature-dependent vibrational spectra and anharmonic scattering rates from first-principles and combining these with Bayesian adjustment of element-specific bonding parameters, the method isolates the phonon contribution without averaging it into a Debye temperature. This decoupling improves the accuracy of lattice conductivity estimation relative to models which merge lattice and electronic contributions.
generation.predicted_outcome: The approach will yield lattice thermal conductivity predictions that deviate from experimental measurements by at least 20% less error than baseline models (which rely on Debye temperature estimates and perfect-crystal assumptions). At low temperatures (<200 K), where electron and lattice contributions are comparable, the lattice-only prediction will match measured values more closely, while at higher temperatures (300–1200 K) the separated predictions will elucidate the impact of oxygen impurities on electronic contributions.
generation.baseline: Prior analytical and DFT-based estimates that approximate heat transport using a single Debye temperature or elastic properties, typically assuming defect-free, perfect bulk crystals without decoupling lattice and electronic conduction.
generation.boundary: The approach is expected to be valid for high-purity, defect-free HfNbTaTiZr in regimes where the phonon spectrum and anharmonicity dominate (e.g., below 200 K) and may require recalibration for polycrystalline or oxygen-contaminated samples at higher temperatures (>300 K).
generation.uncertainty: While a 20% improvement in prediction accuracy is anticipated, uncertainties remain regarding the absolute quantification because of residual challenges in fully capturing electron-phonon coupling and disorder effects in real-world samples.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare high-purity, defect-free HfNbTaTiZr specimens and perform low-temperature (below 200 K) thermal conductivity measurements that enable separation of the lattice and electronic contributions (e.g., via techniques like time-domain thermoreflectance combined with electrical transport measurements). Compare the independently measured lattice thermal conductivity with predictions from both the new decoupled model and traditional conflated models. Additionally, test samples with controlled oxygen levels at higher temperatures (300–1200 K) to verify the distinct impact on electronic conduction.
measurements: Electronic transport properties (e.g., Seebeck coefficient, magnetoresistance)
Microstructural assessment for defects and impurity levels
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the experimentally measured lattice thermal conductivity in oxygen-free samples below 200 K is not predicted with at least a 20% lower error by the new decoupled approach compared to the baseline conflated models, or if the predicted separation of contributions does not hold in controlled high-temperature tests, the hypothesis will be falsified.

## Abstract
While first-principles methods have been successfully applied to characterize individual properties of multi-principal element alloys (MPEA), their use in searching for optimal trade-offs between competing properties is hampered by high computational demands. In this work, we present a framework to explore Pareto-optimal compositions by integrating advanced ab initio-based techniques into a Bayesian multi-objective optimization workflow, complemented by a simple analytical model providing straightforward analysis of trends. We benchmark the framework by applying it to solid solution strengthening and ductility of refractory MPEAs, with the parameters of the strengthening and ductility models being efficiently computed using a combination of the coherent-potential approximation method, accounting for finite-temperature effects, and actively-learned moment-tensor potentials parameterized with ab initio data. Properties obtained from ab initio calculations are subsequently used to extend predictions of all relevant material properties to a large class of refractory alloys with the help of the analytical model validated by the data and relying on a few element-specific para

The group of HEAs has the potential to overcome currently used materials in many applications. Some of them have excellent high temperature properties and are therefore candidates for replacement of Ni-superalloys, which are currently used for turbine blades, etc. []. Cryogenic applications are also potential fields of interest as some HEAs retain high plasticity even at cryogenic temperatures [].
In this work the HfNbTaTiZr (equiatomic) alloy was studied. This alloy has the potential to be used in high temperature applications or as a biocompatible material due to its chemical composition consisting of refractory metals [,,], which are biocompatible [,,] elements. This alloy is usually prepared by an arc melting process [,,,,]. Power metallurgy was studied as an alternative route of HEA synthesis [,,,].
